newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish forestry shares ride on dollar, prices.
newsitem.headline: Swedish forestry shares ride on dollar, prices.

text.p: Despite continued price pressures on pulp, Swedish forestry shares have risen more than five percent in the past three days, riding on the strong dollar and higher prices of some forestry products.
Swedish forestry group Stora AB and Finnish rival UPM Kymmene recently announced price increases for light weight coated (LWC) magazine paper by five percent and five to eight percent respectively.
On Wednesday, Swedish AssiDoman announced it intended to raise prices on kraftliner by ten percent.
"People believe that price increases will keep appearing and you have to catch on," said Erik Magnusson, forestry analyst at Nordbanken.
"It was Salomon Brothers' buy recommendation (on the forestry sector) last week which started the whole buying business."
Hopes for an upturn in the sluggish forestry market and investors turning toward cyclicals supported forestry shares, analysts said.

"There are three key factors, the dollar, increased expectations about a faster than expected upturn in the market and finally a tendency that investors more and more turn to cyclicals," said Hakan Ostling, analyst at Goldman Sachs.
But there could be setbacks as pulp inventories keep rising and prices are rather on a downtrend than an uptrend.
"The pulp price is the joker in the pack," an analyst said. "There could be setbacks if the pulp price is pushed lower."
Thursday's news about a smaller than usual rise in North American and Scandinavian (NorScan) pulp stocks in January could, however, be a positive sign.
Sources reported Norscan stocks rose about 130,000 tonnes last month to around two million tonnes, compared with a normal increase in January of around 200,000 tonnes.
The rise was curbed by an lift in pulp deliveries in the U.S., Europe and Asia, sources said.
"This was very positive," the vice president of Norwegian forestry group Norske Skog Claes-Inge Isacson told Reuters.
"This indicates there has been discipline and restraint among producers," he said, referring to production cutbacks.
At 1400 GMT Thursday, the forestry sector was 1.60 percent higher on the Stockholm Stock Exchange, outperforming a general index advance of 0.6 percent.
Stora was up 1.5 crowns at 103, while AssiDoman gained two to 189 and MoDo rose four to 227. SCA advanced three to 163 but pulp sensitive Rottneros slipped 0.10 to 9.20 crowns
